claims.text: Introducing a MAX-phase compound into a ceramic or metal matrix composite will produce stable self-lubricating behavior over a wide temperature range.
Introducing a MAX-phase compound into a ceramic or metal matrix composite will provide high mechanical strength under extreme conditions.
Ti3SiC2 is an example of a MAX-phase compound suitable for incorporation into the proposed composite.
Incorporating a MAX phase during synthesis introduces a layered lubricating phase into the composite.
The MAX-phase compound will be distributed throughout the matrix while retaining a layered structure.
The layered crystallographic structure of the MAX phase provides intrinsic solid lubrication.
The MAX phase reinforces the mechanical strength of the composite because of its robust physical properties.
The combination of lubrication and reinforcement balances lubrication efficiency with high-temperature strength.
The MAX-phase-containing composite will have a lower friction coefficient across a wide temperature range than a comparable matrix without MAX-phase additives.
The MAX-phase-containing composite will exhibit less wear across a wide temperature range than a comparable matrix without MAX-phase additives.
The MAX-phase-containing composite will maintain or enhance mechanical strength relative to a comparable matrix without MAX-phase additives.
A comparable composite lacking MAX-phase reinforcement fails to maintain both low friction and high strength across the entire temperature range.
Inadequate MAX-phase distribution or interfacial bonding can limit composite performance.
Extreme temperatures may compromise MAX-phase stability and thereby limit performance.
Optimization of lubrication and strength is sensitive to composition, microstructure, processing, and interfacial bonding.
